description: The chart illustrates the number of experts assigned per model layer, with each layer’s total shown as a stacked bar split into two labeled components (G1 and G2). The horizontal axis contains the categories labeled “Layer,” ordered sequentially from 1 to 24 with evenly spaced integer tick marks. The vertical axis is labeled “Number of Experts,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 10 with regularly spaced tick labels at intervals of 2 (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10). Each layer is represented by a stacked bar composed of a small blue base segment (unlabeled in the legend) of approximately 1 expert for every layer, a green segment labeled “G1,” and a yellow segment labeled “G2.” Approximate stacked totals by layer are: layer 1 ≈ 9 (blue 1 + G1 4 + G2 4), layer 2 ≈ 8 (1 + 3 + 4), layer 3 ≈ 6 (1 + 2 + 3), layer 4 ≈ 8 (1 + 3 + 4), layer 5 ≈ 7 (1 + 3 + 3), layer 6 ≈ 5 (1 + 2 + 2), layer 7 ≈ 3 (1 + 1 + 1), layers 8–9 ≈ 5 each (1 + 2 + 2), layer 10 ≈ 4 (1 + 1 + 2), layers 11–15 ≈ 3 each (1 + 1 + 1), layers 16–18 ≈ 5 each (1 + 2 + 2), layers 19–22 ≈ 6 each (1 + 3 + 2), and layers 23–24 ≈ 3 each (1 + 1 + 1). The bars are not sorted by height; they follow the natural layer index order, and no individual bars appear specially emphasized beyond the consistent stacking colors and the legend indicating G1 (green) and G2 (yellow).
